investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the remote agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (the resource quota or physical peer-pod VM slots are exhausted), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 125–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never started, and the eval runner received no usable response, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is an external account/billing configuration failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or the image generation route itself. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 125–147 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never started, and the eval runner received no usable response, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) empty. This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required pods: 2 of 6 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the remote agent VM was never provisioned and the runtime probe never reached the point of returning orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the two eligible nodes. The pod submitted by the eval runner was declared Unschedulable after 147 seconds and preemption was not possible (no victims found, and the 4 remaining nodes are excluded by node affinity/selector). Because the pod never started, the remote agent VM was never created, and the eval produced zero evidence — failing every required-evidence assertion (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ("hello from aura"). This is an eval-layer signal of an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918 — this is the call that submits the pod; it never returned because the pod was never scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these could be satisfied without a running VM.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes, meaning the allocatable VM slots are fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already at capacity, leaving zero schedulable nodes.

Tertiary — stuck or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from being scheduled (no preemption victims found supports this).

Lower confidence — a cluster-level quota or LimitRange on kata.peerpods.io/vm that is set too low for concurrent eval runs across remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime firing in sequence.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduler failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current pod scheduling state for remote-agent pods in the cluster
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep remote-agent
reproductionSteps.details: Identify any pods stuck in Pending or not fully terminated that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.

reproductionSteps.label: Check allocatable and requested kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on all nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm how many VM slots are allocatable per node and how many are currently consumed.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
reproductionSteps.details: Identify which workloads are holding the limited VM slots and whether any are leaked or stuck.

reproductionSteps.label: Review node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm which node labels are required by the remote-agent pod and verify that only 2 nodes carry those labels, matching the scheduler's '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' report.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes VM scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the two affinity-eligible nodes, blocking all remote-agent pod creation. This is the earliest violated boundary in the failure chain (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes that are already at kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: remote-agents feature — all three eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed with the same class of scheduler error, indicating the entire remote-agent provisioning path is blocked in production-api (source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state, failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner branch at line 1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which submits the pod that becomes Unschedulable. The probe never advances past this call, so no evidence is collected (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, failed-check.evidence).

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster immediately for Pending or stuck remote-agent pods consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots; force-delete any that are leaked or no longer needed.
Check the total allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the two affinity-eligible nodes and compare against the number of slots currently requested by running workloads.
Review the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec to determine whether the constraint limiting scheduling to 2 nodes is intentional; if not, consider expanding eligible nodes.

If VM slot capacity is genuinely exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable limit on existing nodes or adding additional affinity-eligible nodes to the cluster.

Confirm whether the remote-agents feature degraded-after-failures threshold (degradedAfterFailures: 1, outageAfterFailures: 2 per infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187-188) has triggered a feature-level degraded or outage status, and communicate accordingly to stakeholders if so.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required: false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), so this check alone does not constitute a required-check outage; however, the two required sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) are both failing, which may trigger the outageAfterFailures threshold.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval in isolation
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the scheduling failure is still present or was transient; a pass would produce the required evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and satisfy the contract.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly confirms whether VM slots are exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes, proving or disproving the primary cause.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List Pending or stuck remote-agent pods
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies leaked or stuck pods that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new scheduling.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels to verify affinity/selector scope
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that only 2 of 6 nodes carry the labels required by the remote-agent pod spec, validating the '4 node(s) didn't match' scheduler message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether concurrent eval runs exhaust the available VM slots, which would indicate a quota or concurrency issue rather than a persistent capacity shortage.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted on the affinity-eligible nodes would disprove the resource exhaustion hypothesis.

A successful re-run of the eval (remote-agent-runtime returning orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) after no cluster changes were made would suggest the failure was transient rather than a sustained capacity constraint.
Evidence that the pod was scheduled but failed for a different reason (e.g., image pull error, OOMKill) would shift the root cause away from scheduler capacity.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state concurrent with this failure window would indicate the issue is isolated to the runtime check's pod spec rather than shared VM capacity.

Cluster node count or kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable values that show sufficient headroom at the time of the failure would suggest a misconfigured node affinity/selector is the sole cause rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent pod creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduler timeout.

Add an eval that detects Pending remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60 seconds) and reports them as leaked, enabling earlier detection of slot exhaustion caused by stuck pods.
Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector, alerting when the eligible node count drops below a safe minimum.
Consider a dedicated eval for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource headroom that warns when available slots fall below the number needed to run all remote-agents sibling checks concurrently.
